item.title: 1 Dead After Student Livestreams School Shooting in the Philippines
item.description: The boy shot and killed a schoolmate at a junior high school before fatally turning the gun on himself, the mayor of Zamboanga City said.

item.title: Kushner Meets Netanyahu in Israel in Effort to Break Logjam Over Gaza
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel has refused to pull back the country’s military until Hamas fully disarms. But the Trump administration is under pressure to show progress.

item.title: How Israel’s Financial Chokehold Is Stifling the West Bank Economy
item.description: Intensifying restrictions have hit every part of the territory’s dealings, spurring worries about whether the Palestinian Authority can remain solvent.

item.title: Houthis Claim Strike on Saudi Vessel as Red Sea Violence Escalates
item.description: The armed group, based in Yemen and backed by Iran, said it had launched missiles near the vital maritime trade route, in a conflict that shows no sign of abating.

item.title: A Mother’s Quest to Rescue Her Son From Russian-Occupied Ukraine
item.description: They made a risky bid to reunite after three years of separation, illness and deprivation — the kind of ordeal suffered by many thousands of families torn apart by the war in eastern Ukraine.

item.title: Chocó, Colombia, Faces Deeper Hardship After an Earthquake
item.description: In Chocó, a remote region, “pain, hunger and homelessness await” survivors of last week’s earthquake, the governor said. Shakira visited to help draw awareness.

item.title: At Ex-Premier Zhu Rongji’s Funeral, China’s Past Shadows Its Present
item.description: Beijing wants to portray today’s China as carrying forward Zhu Rongji’s era of growth, but for many Chinese, the optimism of that time has since faded.

item.title: Barred From Ballot, a Party Becomes a Vessel for Russians’ Discontent
item.description: The spotlight on the country’s only antiwar party has brought a spark to what had looked like another dull, tightly controlled election campaign.

item.title: How Ukraine’s Satellites Help Drive Its War Drones
item.description: Ukrainian drone teams have a powerful new tool: near real-time information on troop movements and locations.

item.title: Zambia Says President Won Re-election After Tumultuous Campaign
item.description: With a second term, Hakainde Hichilema must navigate relations with the Trump administration, which has sought greater access to the copper-rich nation’s natural resources.
